title: The publish history scan is too slow for the 60 s SessionStart hook on a long range
goal: the per-commit history scan of kbgit.py publish caches each source commit's verdict by sha under _cache/ so a range is scanned once, scans only the lines each commit adds, and publish --hook exits 0 quietly with one line ('publish by hand: N commits to check') when the uncached range exceeds a bound it can scan within the hook's timeout; TestPublishHookLongRange in _tools/test_kbpublic.py plants a long range and asserts the hook returns within its bound and a second run uses the cache; reported from a Windows clone where about 500 commits took over 5 minutes
